title: Corner Cycle Continuous Give & Go
description: A continuous corner-cycle station where the first player retrieves a puck on the wall, cycles it to support, then drives the net for a return pass and quick shot.
coaching_points: Communicate for the cycle and the return pass.
Bounce the cycle puck off the wall so it is easy for support to retrieve.
Open the blade early on the off-hand side and shoot off the pass.
Follow the shot and rotate immediately into the next role.

title: 1 v 1, 2 v 2, 3 v 3
description: A competitive cross-ice game that builds from 1-on-1 to 2-on-2 to 3-on-3, then removes players back down to 2-on-2 and 1-on-1.
coaching_points: Players track who is entering and leaving so numbers are recognized immediately.
Defenders keep sticks in passing lanes and angle play outside.
Forwards make quick passes and shoot when lanes open.
Transition instantly as the numbers change on each whistle.

title: 3 v 3 Pass to Coach
description: A 3-on-3 possession game where all three teammates must touch the puck before the team can pass back to the coach for a point.
coaching_points: Players without the puck skate to open space and stay available.
Support the puck carrier from short, useful angles.
Protect possession instead of forcing low-percentage plays.
React quickly after turnovers to regain possession.

title: 2 v 1 Keep Away
description: A 2-on-1 keep-away game in a confined area that develops puck carrying, puck support, deception, and defensive positioning.
coaching_points: Players away from the puck move into open areas and keep sticks ready.
Use deception and puck protection to create passing lanes.
Defender stays between the two attackers with the stick in the lane.
Track completed passes and takeaways to add competition.

title: Sabre Half-Ice 2v2 With Outlets
description: A half-ice 2-on-2 game with support players stationed along the goal line and blue line so puck carriers can use outlets to create offense.
coaching_points: Use hard, quick tape-to-tape passes to the support players.
Keep eyes up and communicate before using an outlet.
Move to open ice immediately after passing.
Use the outlets to create better attacking numbers and spacing.

title: 1 v 1 Race to Puck to 2 v 2
description: Two players race to a loose puck at center. The winner connects to a teammate to begin a 2-on-1 rush while the losing side's support player backchecks, creating a 2-on-2 in-zone battle.
coaching_points: Win body position first during the puck race.
Dot players anticipate whether they are joining offense or backchecking.
Move the puck quickly once possession is won.
Backchecker closes hard to turn the rush into an even-number situation.

title: Use the Nets Puck Protection
description: A defense puck-protection drill using two nets as obstacles. The puck carrier uses the back of the nets as shields to escape a forechecker and deliver a controlled outlet pass.
coaching_points: Use the net as a physical shield from pressure.
Sell fakes with the head, shoulders, hips, and stick.
Protect the puck while changing direction in tight space.
Get eyes up and deliver the outlet once the lane appears.

title: Power Play Game Long Short
description: Two power-play units work on opposite halves of the ice with different net orientations. The active side plays a 5-on-3 until the penalty killers clear the puck to the opposite unit.
coaching_points: Make quick decisions in condensed space.
Use crisp passing to maintain possession under pressure.
Keep power-play spacing organized despite the smaller area.
Penalty killers focus on strong positioning and clean clears.

title: Power Play Face-Off Loss Drill
description: A power-play retrieval drill that starts from a simulated lost offensive-zone faceoff. The unit works to regain inside body position, retrieve the puck, and generate a shot quickly.
coaching_points: Win inside body position on the retrieval.
React immediately after the faceoff loss before the penalty kill can clear.
Move the puck efficiently once it is recovered.
Create the first shot within three passes whenever possible.

title: The D Initiate
description: A transition rush drill where the defenseman initiates the attack with an early pass, joins the rush as the third attacker, and receives the final cross-ice pass for a quick shot.
coaching_points: Defenseman pushes the pace and initiates the rush early.
Forwards gain middle ice on the entry and support underneath the puck.
All players keep sticks ready for passes.
Defenseman joins the attack and shoots quickly on the final pass.
